description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve rural road connectivity to markets and social services, and in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to provide an immediate and effective response.

The development objective of the Rural Connectivity Project for Central African Republic is to improve rural road connectivity to markets and social services, and in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency, to provide an immediate and effective response. The project comprises of four components. The first component, rural roads rehabilitation and maintenance will focus on the rehabilitation of rural roads in two selected intervention areas, in the North-West and North-East of the country. It consists of two sub-components: (i) north-west road rehabilitation; and (ii) north-east road rehabilitation. The second component, project implementation management (PIU) and monitoring will finance institutional strengthening for the PIU, including the hiring of new staff. The third component, resettlement may include: (i) cash compensation for land; (ii) moving allowances; and (iii) temporary income losses directly associated with the rehabilitation of rural roads. The fourth component, contingency emergency response will have an initial zero-dollar allocation. In case this component is activated, it will be completely financed with International Development Association (IDA) funds.

title.narrative: Proportion of improved project roads under routine maintenance

comment.narrative: <p>The targeted proportion of road under routine maintenance (100 percent at appraisal and 50 percent after restructuration) was not achieved as there were no rehabilitated roads under routine maintenance at the time of closure.</p>

<p>The project roads directly served about 36,000 farmers and connected 105,000 rural dwellers to markets, services, and the rest of The Central African Republic road network. This represents 91.3% of the target.</p>

Roads with improved road safety measures

comment.narrative: <p>614 km of rural roads were successfully rehabilitated by the project and these roads spread over the North-West (472 km) and North-East (142 km) regions. Specifically, 218 km of roads in the Ouham and 254 km of roads in the Ouham-Péndé prefectures of the North-West region using Labor Intensive Public Works contracts; and 142 km of the planned 322 km (774 km at appraisal) between Kaga Bandoro and Ndele road in the North-East region.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>614 km of rural roads were successfully rehabilitated with improved road safety measures by the project.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was changed at the restructuration for a reduction in travel time between Kaga Bandoro, and Ndele. Despite the very fragile context and the challenging work environment, UNOPS managed to reopen the road between Kaga Bandoro, and Ndele. That roadsection was inaccessible from 2015 to 2017. Further to its reopening, the average travel time which was about one (01) week, was shortened by one (01) day.</p>

Person-days of employment created through the Labor Intensive Public Works

comment.narrative: <p>The project successfully created 58,300 person-days of employment through Labor Intensive Public Works contracts. These achievements represent respectively 41% and 39% of the original end target, and this is reinforced by the positive reaction of 80 percent of beneficiaries in the project catchment area.</p>
